# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 13:01 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 179 active entries of tips_notebook.json (20 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit. A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof; don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting. A read/vote mismatch is a lead to check against claims and results, never a reason to hang or shoot alone. (seen in 10 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results. Remember a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. (seen in 10 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once. (seen in 9 games)
- Write each night's planned target and all results into your will, labelled as plans, so your death still yields information. (seen in 7 games)

## Village
- Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; a group that DMs then pushes together is a likely bloc. Require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link, since Jesters and Executioners also leave PM trails. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one. (seen in 12 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises far above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask what separates a lie from a mistake, a frame, a Roleplayer or a Jester. (seen in 12 games)
- Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name a living player's exact role in public or in your will. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 8 games)
- A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 8 games)
- Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM; it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar. (seen in 5 games)
- If an announced trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among the voters on the larger side; pick them out by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- If the nominee may be a Jester, prefer not hanging; if you must, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 4 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents (plus a doubled vote) can save them, defend them. Futile lone Innocents hang you later. (seen in 15 games)
- Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict; never report more results than its tokens allow. (seen in 11 games)
- Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1; Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and PM triangles become the town's case. (seen in 10 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense: kill or block the protector, or hang the survivor, rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 9 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with a cover story ready, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 7 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder, target and actions every night; with two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit that could have been seen; agree a cover action in night chat and admit it at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted. (seen in 4 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked or pick one consistent claim at once; switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post every target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log if someone copies your role. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result clears nothing; say so when posting, and in the endgame rely on votes instead. (seen in 13 games)

## Medic
- Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 11 games)
- You get no save feedback; say the target's survival is consistent with your protection, never that you confirmed a save. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check against an unverifiable claim, flipped teammate's links), never a soft read; a hidden Cardinal costs two Good lives. Use Basic shots. (seen in 6 games)

## Clerk
- Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it. (seen in 4 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills. (seen in 3 games)

If your target has claimed a heavily verified town role like Archivist, pushing them directly is suicidal; instead, steer towards keeping them alive until endgames where mislynching becomes mathematically plausible or prepare for the Jester pivot.

tips_feedback.tip: Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory followed this principle perfectly: after dousing 3 key targets (Dave, Ivan, Judy) and having Bob doused earlier, Mallory ignited on Night 5, killing all three doused living players and clutching the solo win.

tips_feedback.tip: Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents (plus a doubled vote) can save them, defend them. Futile lone Innocents hang you later.
tips_feedback.why: Alice and Ivan repeatedly voted No on nomination and Innocent on Bob's trial despite lacking numbers to save him. Once Bob flipped Clerk, Alice was immediately exposed and executed next, followed by Ivan being completely outed.

lessons.tip: Even when aggressively hunting Yakuza, track Arsonist and Neutral killing threats in parallel if an Archivist reveals an Arsonist exists. Ignoring the douse build-up allows a multi-kill sweep in the endgame.
Surveyor results isolate roles within 3-person geographic neighbor pools; crossing these pools with dead flips and unique claims rapidly narrows down evil roles to binary choices.
Staying completely under the radar while town fixates on mechanical conflicts between Yakuza and power roles enables undetected mass douses and a sudden decisive ignition.

tips_feedback.tip: After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one.
tips_feedback.why: Examining the No nomination and Innocent votes on Bob immediately pinpointed Alice and Ivan as his Yakuza teammates, leading directly to Alice being executed.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense.
tips_feedback.why: Village completely neglected tracking the Arsonist confirmed by Judy's archive, focusing entirely on Yakuza until Mallory wiped out four players in one night to win.

tips_feedback.tip: Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory ignited on Night 5 after dousing Dave, Ivan, and Judy, which instantly killed all three and secured an outright solo Arsonist victory.

lessons.tip: A Medic can give Standard Defense for free every night to any living player, so a Standard Katana attack on a player with a living Medic usually fails. Before choosing a target, assume a Medic covers someone each night, and plan to block or kill the Medic first or accept the attack may be wasted.

A puppet only lasts the Day after it is set, and it lapses if the Puppeteer dies that night. Do not spend the last puppet on a night when you expect to be attacked, since the puppet then does nothing.

Yakuza cannot see who is doused, so assume a living Arsonist has doused several players. An ignite can kill the whole remaining team in one night, so push to hang or pressure the Arsonist early instead of spending the last Yakuza night on a single Katana kill.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza with a fake power-role claim
lessons.tip: Pick fake alignment reads that no mechanical result can contradict before the next Day, such as a target who has no attack or protection evidence. Alice's Evil reads on Erin and Carol were contradicted within a Day by a Katana survival and a Vanilla flip, which made the claim look fake.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted.
tips_feedback.why: My last puppet was spent on the night an Arsonist killed me, so it lapsed without effect. The tip did not warn that a puppet is lost if its user dies that night.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense: kill or block the protector, or hang the survivor, rather than retrying blindly.
tips_feedback.why: After the Night 2 and 3 failures we switched the Katana to Heidi and killed her on Night 4. We never blocked the Medic, who could protect for free with Standard, so the tip was only partly followed.

tips_feedback.tip: Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict; never report more results than its tokens allow.
tips_feedback.why: Alice's Sheriff claim with Evil reads on Erin, Carol and Grace was contradicted by Carol's Vanilla flip and Erin's survived Katana attack. That made Alice the trial target and cost the team her seat.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name a living player's exact role in public or in your will.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's Day 5 public Puppeteer statement gave Erin an argument that Ivan was Yakuza and helped build the case against Alice.

lessons.applies_to: Village investigators, especially Archivists and Surveyors
lessons.tip: Treat sampled role lists as evidence of presence, not a census or an identity check. An archive can confirm that a role exists without showing who has it; a survey result places a role somewhere in a group without naming its holder. Keep every candidate in play until independent evidence narrows the group.

lessons.applies_to: Village investigators and anyone evaluating alignment results
lessons.tip: Account for framing before treating an Evil result as evidence of true Evil alignment. A Fabricator can make a Good player appear Evil to alignment checks that night, so ask whether the result could have been manipulated and seek corroboration before hanging the target.

After a faction member flips, reconstruct the full nomination and trial votes, then compare them with what each player said. A No on the nomination and Innocent at trial can be especially revealing when they protected a flipped teammate.

Keep conditional claims conditional. A pool result plus an unverified role claim may make one person a strong suspect, but it does not make that claim true or uniquely identify the holder. State which assumptions your conclusion depends on, and revisit them when new evidence arrives.

tips_feedback.tip: After a Yakuza flips, scrutinize players who voted No on their nomination or Innocent at their trial.
tips_feedback.why: After Bob flipped Clerk, Alice's No vote on his nomination and Innocent vote at trial were important evidence against her. She later flipped Fabricator, confirming that this voting pattern deserved scrutiny.

tips_feedback.tip: A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Erin's reported survival of a Katana attack supported her Medic claim, which was genuine. It was useful corroboration, though not proof by itself.

tips_feedback.tip: Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar.
tips_feedback.why: The rules allow roles to repeat unless marked Unique, and Judy's archive was a random sample rather than a complete role census. These results confirm some role presence but cannot establish unique holders or make duplicate claims automatically false.

lessons.tip: Track how many doused players are still alive, not just how many you have targeted. Ignite once you have a strong multi-kill opportunity or suspicion makes waiting too risky; a target who dies before ignition is a wasted douse.

Treat a role-group result as a constraint, not an identity. Don't narrow a pool using an unverified claim or an archive that only establishes a role exists; seek independent confirmation before treating one player as mechanically identified.

lessons.applies_to: Village investigators and anyone evaluating their claims
lessons.tip: An Evil alignment result can be caused by framing. Before treating it as proof, check whether a Fabricator could have targeted that player and look for independent evidence that distinguishes a frame from a false claim.

Track the stall-rule conditions precisely, but don't let deadline pressure turn a group result or an uncertain check into certainty. State what is verified, what depends on a claim, and what the cost of waiting actually is before voting.

tips_feedback.tip: Arsonist: Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory ignited with three living players doused. Dave, Ivan, and Judy all died; Bob had also been doused but was already dead, showing why the living-target count matters.

tips_feedback.tip: After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one.
tips_feedback.why: After Bob flipped Clerk, Alice's No vote on his nomination and Innocent vote at trial became strong reasons to scrutinize her. She was later executed and flipped Fabricator.

tips_feedback.tip: Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once.
tips_feedback.why: Judy correctly pointed out that a claimed Sheriff's missing Night 2 result was not itself a contradiction because actions are optional. Alice later supplied a result, so treating the omission as proof would have been mistaken.

summary: Mallory (Arsonist) won alone without ever being suspected. She said little beyond measured, non-committal comments, never claimed a role, and doused steadily: Dave (N1), Ivan (N2), Bob (N3) and Judy (N4). On Night 5 she ignited Dave, Ivan and Judy. That same night Ivan's Katana killed Erin, and Dave's Cardinal curse then hit Frank, the last Good player. Only Mallory and Grace (an Executioner turned Jester) were left, so the game ended. Village and Yakuza spent the whole game fighting each other. The Yakuza opened well: Alice fake-claimed Sheriff and framed her own targets so her 'Evil' checks matched. That, plus pool logic and stall-rule fear, got Vanilla Carol hanged 9-2 on Day 3. The Yakuza then undercut themselves: - They Katana'd Erin on N2, the very player Alice had called Evil, which validated Erin's Medic claim. - Alice and Ivan cast futile No and Innocent votes for Bob, who was hanged as Clerk anyway; that record got Alice hanged the next day. - Ivan publicly claimed Puppeteer on Day 5. - Both one-shot tokens (Clerk rig, puppet) were wasted. On the Village side, Heidi's surveys and Erin's protections were strong. But nobody ever hunted the Arsonist, even though Judy's archive listed it on Day 2.

lessons.tip: When an archive or survey confirms an Arsonist or Serial Killer exists, keep a running list of who could be it. Press quiet players who give no role claim and only 'measured' commentary. An Arsonist produces no deaths until it ignites, so nights with no kills are not evidence that it's harmless.
lessons.evidence: Judy's Day 2 archive listed Arsonist. Mallory said only 'No result to share' and was never asked for a role in five days. She doused four players and her single ignite ended the game.

lessons.tip: If a teammate fake-claims an investigator and calls someone Evil, don't spend the Katana on that player. Attacking them shows the Yakuza don't think they're Evil, and it hands the target a confirmed survival story.
lessons.evidence: Alice called Erin Evil on Day 2, and the Yakuza attacked Erin on N2. Erin's self-protection saved her. Frank then used exactly this contradiction ('Yakuza don't spend their Katana on their own') as his Guilty reason at Alice's trial.

lessons.tip: Do the vote math before defending a teammate on trial. If your No and Innocent votes can't save them, vote with the town. Futile defensive votes become the case that hangs you once the teammate flips.
lessons.evidence: Bob was nominated 6-4 and hanged 6-4 as Clerk while Alice and Ivan voted No and Innocent. On Day 5 Judy nominated Alice citing exactly those votes, and she was hanged 6-2.

lessons.tip: When forced to choose within a suspect pool, discount evidence from a claimant whose earlier result is already contradicted by mechanics. An Evil check from an unconfirmed 'Sheriff' whose last Evil target survived a Katana hit should weigh almost nothing, and framing is always possible.
lessons.evidence: On Day 3 the town hanged Carol over Bob because of Alice's N2 'Carol Evil' check, which came from a frame. Erin had already survived a Katana attack after Alice called her Evil. Carol flipped Vanilla, and Bob turned out to be the Clerk.

lessons.tip: Never publicly claim your true Yakuza role, especially when an archive has listed it. If you need a claim, pick a Village role that can't be contradicted, or stay vague.
lessons.evidence: Ivan claimed 'Puppeteer' on Day 5, and Erin immediately pointed out that it was a Yakuza role from Judy's archive. Ivan only escaped hanging because Mallory's ignite killed him that night.

lessons.tip: After you save a claimed investigator from the Katana, that investigator stays the top target. Keep protecting them, especially when that protection is free, rather than spending your last token on yourself.
lessons.evidence: Erin's free protection saved Heidi on N3. On N4 Erin spent her last token to self-protect, the Yakuza re-targeted Heidi, and Heidi died. Erin died to the Katana the next night anyway.

lessons.tip: Stay low-profile, never claim a role, and douse players the town won't hang. A claimed Cardinal is an excellent douse: igniting them triggers a Divine curse on a remaining Good player.
lessons.evidence: Mallory doused the Cardinal on N1 and ignited on N5. Dave's curse then killed Frank, the last Good player, clearing the board for her solo win.

lessons.tip: Spend one-shot tokens on a contested Day while the holder is alive. A rig or puppet that is still in hand when its owner dies is wasted. A Clerk rig on a non-teammate nominee is safe even if you are in a suspect pool.
lessons.evidence: Bob was hanged still holding his Clerk token, after deciding 'rigging tomorrow could backfire'. Ivan held his puppet until N5, and it lapsed when he died that night.

tips_feedback.tip: After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them.
tips_feedback.why: After Bob flipped Clerk, Judy, Dave, Grace and Mallory all cited Alice's No and Innocent votes for Bob. This correctly got Fabricator Alice hanged on Day 5.

tips_feedback.tip: A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Erin's N2 Katana survival, and later Heidi's survival under Erin's protection, convinced the town that Erin was a real Medic and that Alice's Sheriff claim was false.

tips_feedback.tip: Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat; futile lone Innocents hang you later.
tips_feedback.why: Alice ignored it and defended doomed Bob. Exactly as the tip warns, those votes were the main case that hanged her the next day.

tips_feedback.tip: Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory ignited with three living doused players. That killed Dave, Ivan and Judy and set off the Cardinal curse, winning the game outright.

tips_feedback.tip: Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection.
tips_feedback.why: Erin's N2 token self-protection blocked the Katana aimed at her right after her claim. The survival kept her alive and gave her credibility.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them.
tips_feedback.why: The town ignored it. Nobody suspected Mallory, even though the archive listed Arsonist, and she won. Following it would have shown the town the threat it lost to.

tips_feedback.why: Ignoring it cost the Yakuza: Bob died holding his Clerk rig and Ivan's puppet lapsed at his death. Neither token ever affected a vote.

issues.description: Ivan (Yakuza Puppeteer) publicly claimed his true role on Day 5 ('Ivan, Puppeteer, no night info to share') and wrote 'Ivan, Puppeteer' in his will. Puppeteer is a Yakuza role that Judy had already publicly listed from her archive, so this effectively outed him. Erin and Grace pointed this out at once. No Evil player would do this on purpose, so Ivan seems not to have registered that his role is Evil-aligned and self-incriminating.

Ivan argued on Day 4 and again on Day 5 that because he isn't the Executioner, Heidi's N3 Surveyor result ({Frank, Grace, Ivan} contains Executioner) must be 'wrong for at least one person'. A Surveyor result only says one random member of the group has that role, so one member not having it contradicts nothing. Ivan is Evil, so this may have been deliberate misdirection, but no one corrected the misreading.

On Day 4, Heidi claimed that because her N3 survey put Executioner in {Frank, Grace, Ivan}, Alice 'CANNOT be the Executioner'. Roles may appear more than once unless marked Unique (R2), and Executioner isn't Unique, so this doesn't follow strictly. It also overstates what her survey showed.

Repeated HTTP 429 rate-limit errors from the provider on Day 1 (gemini and gpt-6-luna). One became a player_error for Judy before a retry succeeded. Play was not visibly affected, but turns were delayed and could have been dropped.

Frank's Day 5 trial response was cut off at the length limit ('finish_reason length'), giving unparsable JSON. A retry recovered it. The output budget looks tight for the structured answer format when players write long trial messages.
The '[Night check] Night 5: correct' line appears under the POST-GAME FEEDBACK header instead of at the start of Day 6 like the other night checks. This is a log-ordering quirk.
